Theoretical prediction of the thermodynamic behavior of aqueous electrolytes by high pressures and temperatures; IV, Calculation of activity coefficients, osmotic coefficients, and apparent molal and standard and relative partial molal properties to 600 degrees C and 5kb. American Journal of Science 281, 1249-1516.

transcription.from: the published article (PDF from ajsonline.org, a scan): Eqs. (124)-(125), p. 1297, Table 2 (p. 1298) and Table 3 (p. 1304), read on the page images
transcription.note: The radii were in src/equilibrium/activities.jl before this file existed and agree with the r_e,j column of Table 3, all twenty-seven. The package also attributed its default Debye-Hueckel A and B (0.5114 and 0.3288) to Table 1 of this article; Table 1 (p. 1294) gives 0.5091 and 0.3283 at 25 C and 1 bar, and those defaults now come from Parkhurst and Appelo (2013).

nacl_distance_of_closest_approach.description: Distance of closest approach of the ions of NaCl, in Angstrom, calculated from Eq. (125) and the radii of Table 3: the ion-size parameter of a NaCl solution.

notes: Species are keyed by their PHREEQC formula. The radii are effective electrostatic radii r_e,j; the ion-size parameter of an electrolyte k is a_k = 2 sum_j nu_j,k r_e,j / nu_k, Eq. (125), which Table 2 evaluates.

Table 2 is transcribed for the chlorides of the cations of Table 3 and the sodium salts of its anions, the electrolytes an ion forms with a NaCl background. Its lithium salts are left out: they are all 0.02 A below what Eq. (125) gives with the r_e of Li+ printed in Table 3 (1.64), as if Table 2 had used 1.62.
